items.evidence: WITHDRAWN (vanilla changed: the game_rule registry arrived in 1.21.11 with snake_case ids). Vanilla 1.21.11's GameRules clinit (net.minecraft.world.level.gamerules.GameRules — moved to the gamerules subpackage) registers 59 rules with SNAKE_CASE ids into BuiltInRegistries.GAME_RULE; name-for-name diff against the port's RULES table (gamerules.rs:52-130): 59 = 59, zero differences either way. Sampled defaults match vanilla exactly (fire_spread_radius_around_player 128, random_tick_speed 3, max_entity_cramming 24, max_command_forks 65536, max_command_sequence_length 65536, max_block_modifications 32768, max_snow_accumulation_height 1, max_minecart_speed 8). The oracle's tree export confirms the command surface: 116 gamerule literals = 58 available rules x plain + minecraft: forms (max_minecart_speed feature-gated out). The fire-pair collapse that cost 1.21.10 a count difference is gone: vanilla 1.21.11 has no doFireTick / allowFireTicksAwayFromPlayer pair — the single fire_spread_radius_around_player int IS vanilla's form. The template carries NO vanilla_key / from_vanilla_key camelCase mapping (unlike the 1.21.10 child) — it doesn't need one: the engine table IS vanilla's table, including for level.dat persistence. Corpus carries 492 gamerule cases (report §2), including camelCase negative controls that fail on BOTH sides.

items.title: /gamerule exposes the 26.3 snake_case table; vanilla 1.21.10 uses camelCase names — WITHDRAWN: vanilla 1.21.11's game_rule registry uses snake_case ids

items.evidence: REPRODUCES (both parts). Vanilla 1.21.11 still has the OLD selector parser — the option-state refactor (InvertableSetOptionState, SetOnceOptionState) that closed this defect for 26.2 had NOT happened yet in 1.21.11 (neither class exists in the 1.21.11 server-game jar). (a) Duplicate options: vanilla 1.21.11's EntitySelectorOptions.get() (net.minecraft.commands.arguments.selector.options.EntitySelectorOptions) runs the canUse gate BEFORE the value is read — parseOptions calls get() at offset 65, right after readString, before the = and value (Selector.javap:661-730) — but does NOT roll back: only the unknown-option branch does setCursor(start) (offsets 47-52); the inapplicable branch throws ERROR_INAPPLICABLE_OPTION at the cursor as it stands, i.e. at the END of the option name (before =). Rust rolls back to the option-name START (selector.rs:331-341, rollback(reader, start, ...)). For @e[type=pig,type=cow] the cursors differ by the option-name length (4 for type). (b) @a[type=player]: vanilla 1.21.11's type option canUse is !parser.isTypeLimited() (lambda$bootStrap$47), and @a/@p/@r all call limitToType(EntityType.PLAYER) during parseSelector (offsets 165, 196, 225), so vanilla REJECTS @a[type=player] with ERROR_INAPPLICABLE_OPTION. Rust pushes minecraft:player into s.types for @a/@p/@r (selector.rs:218-242) without marking type_option, so can_use("type") stays true and Rust ACCEPTS it.
items.title: Selector option errors: wrong cursor on duplicates; type= accepted for @a/@p/@r

items.evidence: CLOSED (inverted by a vanilla change — the Time argument IS 1.21.11's form). items.title: /worldborder time uses a Time argument where vanilla uses an integer — CLOSED: vanilla 1.21.11 uses Time

items.evidence: NEW (run-found; minted from the run). 10 give mismatches at perm 4 (3 ok-differs + 7 cursor-differs, same at perm 2). Vanilla 1.21.11's ContainerComponent codec requires each entry to be a ContainerItem with a slot (int) and an item (ItemStack): give @s minecraft:shulker_box[container=[{id:"minecraft:stone",count:64}]] fails in vanilla with Malformed 'minecraft:container' component: 'No key item in MapLike[{count:64,id:"minecraft:stone"}]; No key slot in MapLike[{count:64,id:"minecraft:stone"}]' (cursor 40). Rust ACCEPTS it (decode_component in item.rs:25-95 has NO minecraft:container arm — it falls through to _ => Ok(()), so any container value parses, including the 26.x {id, count} shape and the components:{...}-nested variant). The Rust codebase itself knows the 1.21.11 shape — snbt.rs:1027 tests {{slot:0,item:{item}}} — but the parse-time decoder never enforces it. Same class as G07a/G08 (component codec validation gap), distinct root cause. Affects every item argument carrying a container component (/give, /item, /loot, /summon with equipment), not just /give. Fix form: a minecraft:container arm in decode_component requiring a list of compounds each with an int slot and a decodable item.
items.title: Item minecraft:container component accepts entries without slot/item; vanilla 1.21.11 rejects them
